source: That one's not very friendly. Nicked my wrist once.
Oh, I rarely see this one out and about. She's always hiding.
This one's grown large and happy. Irma must have taken a liking to it.
Bernardo and the rest of the guards have all but adopted this one.
She seems to like lingering in the guard quarters a little too often, hoping for scraps.
A sprightly little dog. I wonder whom it belongs to?
This hound's nearly always underfoot.
He looks awfully content. Wonder which flowerbed he's gone and dug up.
Hello, little hound! Have you been chasing hares?
Hamlet's gone and blocked out all the light. How juvenile.
If I want to sleep a while, it should be in my own room.
If I want to take a nap, it should be in my own room.
This is where the Queen has her hair done. A mirror of this size must have taken a long while to build.
Oh, Laertes... What could you possibly need all these blades for?
Elsinore castle looks enormous, even this far away.
It may look shallow, but it's deceptively deep.
I used to play here as a girl. Now, though, with all these heavy skirts... better steer clear.
These were carved, I'm told, after the last time Elsinore was sieged and rebuilt.
It's the Danish coat of arms.
It's late, I should really go to bed.
I have no reason to head to the docks right now.
That way lies eastward, out into the Sound.
Denmark controls the waterway here. All passing ships must stop and pay their tolls to us.
The Royal Fleet of Denmark is anchored close by. This harbor is rather shallow, so longboats come ashore to ferry passengers to and fro.
It's a note bearing the Seal of the King.
Hamlet's looking at it right now. I can't get close.
'I've entrusted these orders to two loyal servants, Rosencrantz and Guildenstern, to ensure that...'
'...To be executed upon arrival.'
This is a death warrant for Hamlet, written by Claudius. It'll never reach England now.
Still, I wonder if... Rosencrantz and Guildenstern were carrying this letter intentionally.
My assumption is deception on all sides.
That way leads to the stables. Nothing in there but a lot of muck and mares.
That way leads into the fields. I can see the hills roll for miles. Regardless, I've no interest in leaving town.
If I knew how to steer a ship, I could go anywhere.
But as is, I would probably only wind up at the bottom of the ocean.
There's so little light in here.
This is where prisoners sleep. Or... try to sleep, I'd guess.
What just— What did we—
Is he... dead?
...It's quiet.
No Hamlet in my room this time. Something's definitely changed.
I wonder if Father's outside.
Still don't care for this place, even now.
Don't think you can fool me, Ophelia.
I see. It's the same as before. You're still here.
Still here? I was about to say the same about you!
You're going to miss the party. Everyone else is already in the great hall.
Your brother suggested we ought to let you sleep... but I'm glad to see you refreshed and ready.
Come downstairs when you're ready, won't you?
What's going on?
This is all new.
There's... it can't be. This must be another trick.
There's my girl.
Finally awake, O lazy sister of mine?
Ophelia! OooOOOoh, Ophelia!...
Uh, you'll have to pardon mother.
We all began drinking a... bit much waiting for you to rouse. The wine's been out for hours.
I'm so haaaappy! I love a good summer feast.
Now, love, can we finally begin?
I know you wanted to wait for Ophelia. Well, here she is. Let's not let the food grow cold.
Please. I'm starving to death. I'm not long for this world.
Guilda, we just had sweetmeats—not an hour ago, too.
But have you seen the table? Irma outdid herself. I can't wait another second! I'll die!
Finally, someone who likes to eat my food as much as I like to make it.
You all are having a party? What of the morning court session? What of Fortinbras?
Fortinbras? You mean the Prince of Norway?
What of him, Ophelia?
He... well, the... diplomatic effort. Didn't he... isn't he threatening Denmark?
What? Sire, have I missed something?
I don't think so. I'm not sure what you mean, Ophelia. But I have noticed there's no goblet in your hand. Hmm!
Come! Drink! Be merry! And that's a royal order.
Er, mother, do you need to be tucked into bed? You're drifting off.
Don't mind her, Hamlet. Let her sleep if she wants to. She'll wake up as the night goes on.
I'll watch over her, m'lord. I'll call for yeh if she wakes! Uh, assumin' I'm not drunk myself.
She seems remarkably happy tonight, doesn't she, uncle? The happiest since, well...
Since Father's illness took him.
Aye, she does.
I wish his health hadn't declined so quickly. I loved my brother. I wanted him to live. For her sake, and for yours.
It wasn't your fault. There was nothing to be done. Plague steals indiscriminately.
My father was a good man. And you—you're the closest to him I have now. All will be well in time.
I'll drink to that, nephew.
(This is so strange. Did history itself change?)
(Claudius isn't a murderer in this world, at the very least...)
Laertes. Aren't you sailing for Paris?
Oh! About that. for some reason, I couldn't sleep last night, and I got to thinking about it.
I believe I'll stay in Elsinore a while longer. There's time enough for travel later on.
How often does such a bright, warm summer as this come to visit Denmark, after all?
Well, that's wonderful. I'm sure Brit will be very happy, too.
Happy that he's staying? It's not the worst, I suppose.
(Listen, Ophelia. Just between you and me, I've got a little surprise in mind tonight.)
(Wait and see.)
Come, Ophelia. Let me show you to your seat. Shall we dine?
Of course.
Everyone, I've a toast to make.
Hear, hear!
Of course, Laertes.
I'd like to toast to health, to life, and to love.
And to this brilliant, wonderful woman—whom I love, and who has loved me in return.
Wha? Me?
To some, our relationship has been known a long time. To others, it may be—er—more of a surprise.
I'll say.
Why have I never heard of this before?
Laertes, you don't have to.
Tonight, I'd like to ask Lady Birgitta for her hand in marriage.
Ah! Yesh! Yesh!
Well, I'll be damned. Certainly took him long enough.
Laertes! This is highly irregular!
Oh, come now, Father. They're a suitable match of sufficient rank.
What have you to fear?
W-well, nothing, but I—I haven't spoken to or met her father, and I haven't asked his mind, and—
And well, the dowry, and...
Brit, I love you. I don't want to travel the world without you.
If there's any way you share those feelings... if you think you could... share your life...
I accept, you idiot. Of course. You didn't have to be so public, though.
Invite them all into our bedroom too while you're at it, why don't you?
Hmph. Well then. Let me not to the marriage of true minds admit impediments.
If this is your wish, then...
We're going to have a wedding!
Congratulations, brother. I'm happy to see you happy.
I must admit, I'm relieved. I wasn't sure how you and Father would take the news.
Let's not let the night end.
I've already talked to Bernardo and Hamlet. Whenever we can slip away, the three of us are planning to meet by the pond.
You want to slip away? But everyone's still here.
Oh, it's a welcome celebration, but I can only take so much drunk revelry.
A quieter venue fits the mood. You should come. It's been so long since the four of us got together.
Yes. I'd... I'd like that.
I'll be there.
This is it.
He's gone. I can scarcely believe it. Everything is the way it was meant to be.
Well, I'm going to be staggering back to my room tonight.
As well you should be. Tonight's cause for celebration.
And cause to drink to the death of Brit's taste in men.
You're just upset she doesn't like you.
It's quite all right. I've grown used to that unrequited feeling.
Not for her, though.
It's been a long time since the four of us were out here like this.
Too long. Why don't we ever have fun like this anymore? Did we forget how once we grew up?
I suppose so.
Well, I'd say it's the three of you who grew. I never had much luck with that.
Sorry, Wee One.
I detest that nickname.
As I recall, it was your brother who gave it to you. I'm merely reusing it.
That was the summer he called me The Ogre. Such an unpleasant phase for us all.
I can't help that I'm so terribly good with nomenclature.
I love you all.
I've been-- it's been-- I've watched you all die so many times.
I didn't know what else to do. I was so scared. So desperate.
But I finally fixed it. I was persistent. I did everything right. I fixed everything. And now you're here.
Everything's right again.
Ophelia? Are you all right?
She looks like she's falling asleep. She's not making any sense.
I can escort her back to her room.
No, no... leave her. She loves to be here by the pond. It's a warm night with a full moon. She'll be all right.
You know, ever since the castle's been in mourning, it hasn't felt the same.
I agree. There's been a terrible cloud over things. I'm certain that's what Ophelia means.
But today, for the first time, I had the thought that perhaps that period is coming to a close.
Perhaps things will be well again.
I'm starting to believe that myself, Bernardo.
In fact, I'll toast again to that. Shall we go find some wine?
Excellent plan. And some cards, too.
Goodnight, Ophelia.
Sweet dreams.
Oh. I'm alone.
Must've fallen asleep.
Wonder if the others are still playing cards.
Is that Brit?
She just passed out. In the dirt, no less.
Brit! Wake up.
She's cold.
No. It can't be.
It can't be...
Is that-- cheering?
Encore! Encore!
Yes, please! Don't keep your audience waiting!
I've seen this performance before, but I can't help but sit through it again.
I didn't help write this one, so I must admit, even I don't know the ending.
Look! She's here!
Quick, stop!
The others, outside. They're all dead.
Someone needs to examine them. My lord. My lady. Please.
What? Oh, yes, we know all about them. Disregard it for now.
Yes, dearest, leave them. The crows will get to them eventually. Or the dogs.
Now get on that stage, girl.
Ophelia, I'm so proud of you. If only your mother could be here to see you.
M-me? Get on the stage?
